title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference	s applied-ML evaluation practices into a single, operational reference for model onboarding, prompt-set construction and benchmarking, quantization profile design, and regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, and SREs responsible for model quality and production stability.

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable onboarding checklist for new models entering the Redwood serving catalog.
- Standardize prompt sets and benchmark suites so regressions are detected early and consistently.
- Define quantization profiles and acceptance criteria to balance cost and quality.
- Establish a regression triage flow with escalation thresholds and ownership.

Success metrics (examples):
- Regression detection coverage >= 95% across prioritized prompt sets for top-10 customer use cases.
- Median token latency within catalog SLO +/-10% after quantization when profiled.
- False-positive alert rate for quality regressions < 5% per month.

Audience and scope:
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployment onboards that use the Redwood eval harness.
- Excludes research-only prototype models that are not intended for serving.

Key roles and ownership:
- Model Owner: primary contact for model onboarding and post-rollout issues (e.g., "@owner-team").
- Evaluation Lead: maintains prompt sets, orchestrates benchmark runs, and owns regression alerts (typically Applied ML team).
- Serving Owner: responsible for runtime performance, capacity, and canary deployments (eng-serving-runtime).
- Incident Owner: on-call SRE who triages production quality incidents.

Quick reference table (owners):
| Responsibility | Team | Primary contact example |
|---------------|------|-------------------------|
| Onboarding checklist execution | Applied ML | Asha Patel |
| Prompt-set maintenance | Applied ML | Riley Chen |
| Quantization profiles | Research/Serving Runtime | Miguel Torres |
| Regression triage | SRE / Applied ML | Priya Narang |

1) Model onboarding checklist (step-by-step)
1.1 Pre-onboard artifacts (owner: Model Owner)
- Model card: architecture, tokenizer, intended tasks, training data summary, known biases/limitations.
- Baseline perf profiles: CPU/GPU memory, cold start time, KV cache characteristics.
- Initial acceptance tests: sample prompt set run, perplexity and expected output examples.

1.2 Local eval harness run (owner: Evaluation Lead)
- Run standard eval harness: `./eval_harness/run_all.sh --model <model-id> --output ./reports/<model-id>/`
- Capture: accuracy/f1/bleu (task dependent), calibration, toxicity and safety checks, and latency distribution.
- Attach generated reports and sample outputs to the model card.

1.3 Prompt set curation (owner: Evaluation Lead)
- Create three tiers of prompt sets: Tier A (core customer intents), Tier B (edge cases and long-tail), Tier C (stress tests / synthetic adversarial).
- For each prompt, include: canonical input, expected output or rubric, pass/fail criteria, and priority tag.
- Maintain prompt sets in the repo: `confluence/prompt-sets/<model-id>/` and source control with review PRs.

1.4 Benchmarks and SLO mapping (owner: Serving Owner + Evaluation Lead)
- Define latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and token cost targets for the model. Example: p95 <= 120ms for small-sequence chat baseline.
- Map prompt-set results to business SLOs: e.g., "core intent accuracy >= 92%".

2) Prompt-sets and benchmarking standards
- Prompts must be labeled with metadata: language, seq_length_estimate, customer_priority, task_type, and rubric_id. Example metadata header:
  # metadata: {language: en, seq_length_estimate: short, customer_priority: high, task_type: intent-classification, rubric_id: rubric-12}
- Benchmarks must be reproducible: store seeds, tokenizer version, model commit/tag, and config used.
- Use deterministic evaluation when possible (fixed sampling seed, temperature=0). For stochastic tests, run N=20 seeds and report mean+std.

CLI example for running a benchmark suite:
```
./eval_harness/runner.py --suite core_intents --model-id rwd/model-v2 --tokenizer v1 --seed 42 --output reports/model-v2/core_intents.json
```

Reporting requirements:
- Each run produces a JSON summary and an HTML human-readable report. JSON fields required: run_id, model_id, commit_hash, metrics (flat map), prompt_counts, seed, start_time, end_time.
- Attach reports in the model onboarding PR.

3) Quantization profile guidance
- Purpose: reduce GPU memory and token cost with bounded quality regression.
- Profiles: FP16 (baseline), INT8 dynamic, INT8 Static-Calibration, Q4_K_Mixed.
- Acceptance criteria for a quantized profile:
  - Core intent accuracy drop <= 1.5% absolute vs FP16 baseline on Tier A prompts.
  - Latency reduction >= 10% or memory reduction >= 20% compared to FP16.
  - No new high-severity safety failures introduced.

Quantization testing procedure (owner: Quantization owner / Research):
1. Generate calibration dataset: 5k representative prompts (prioritized by customer volume).
2. Run calibration and produce profile: `./quantize/profile_generator.py --model <model> --calib ./calib.json --out profile.qpf`
3. Evaluate profile using eval harness: `./eval_harness/run_all.py --model <model> --quant_profile profile.qpf --output ./reports/quant/<model>/`
4. Compare metrics and sign off if acceptance criteria are satisfied.

Quantization config table (example):
| Profile name | Method | Calibration required | Expected memory delta | Target use case |
|--------------|--------|----------------------|-----------------------|------------------|
| FP16         | FP16   | no                   | 0%                    | Baseline         |
| INT8-static  | PTQ    | yes (5k calib)       | -40%                  | Cost-sensitive   |
| INT8-dyn     | QAT/other | no                 | -30%                  | Latency-first    |

4) Regression triage playbook
Triggering events (examples):
- Daily regression job detects > 2% absolute drop in core metric for Tier A prompts.
- Customer-reported quality incident with reproducible failing prompt set.
- Canary deployment fails acceptance checks.

Triage steps (ordered):
1. Acknowledge alert and assign Incident Owner (SRE / Evaluation Lead).
2. Reproduce the failure locally using the exact model tag and prompt set. Use `--seed` and `--tokenizer` matching production.
3. Classify regression: model-quality, quantization-related, serving/inference bug, or data/regression in prompt definitions.
4. If model-quality: run a bisect across recent model commits and prompt set versions.
   - Bisect command pattern: `./eval_harness/bisect.py --range <commit1>..<commitN> --suite core_intents`
5. If quantization-related: revert to FP16 or previous acceptable profile and triage quantization pipeline.
6. If serving bug: collect runtime traces, stack, and GPU logs and escalate to serving-runtime.
7. Communicate to stakeholders within 2 hours for Sev>=2 incidents and provide a remediation plan.

Severity matrix and escalation targets:
- Sev1: production-wide customer impact on core intents -> Pager + 1-hour mitigations with rollback.
- Sev2: subset of customers or significant regression in high-priority Tier A -> Page + 4-hour remediation.
- Sev3: non-urgent or low-priority regressions -> Ticket and 3-day SLA for initial response.

5) Dashboards, alerts and instrumentation (owner: Observability/Applied ML)
Minimum dashboards to maintain:
- Daily regression summary: top failing prompts, metric deltas, model tag.
- Canary rollout dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, per-prompt pass rate.
- Quantization comparison dashboard: side-by-side metrics for FP16 vs active quant profiles.

Alert rules (examples):
- regressions/daily/core_intents_drop: fires when Tier A accuracy drops > 2% absolute vs baseline for 24h job.
- canary/failure_rate > 1% for > 5m -> auto-roll back canary.

6) Rollout and canary guidance
- Canary size: start at 1% of traffic for Tier A customer traffic, expand 5x every 30 minutes if no regressions.
- Acceptance checks during canary: pass rate on Tier A prompt set >= baseline - 1.5%, p95 latency within SLO band.
- Automatic rollback rules: any Sev1/regression detected or canary failure rule triggers rollback.

7) Communication and postmortem requirements
- For all Sev1/2 incidents: public incident timeline + internal root-cause draft within 48 hours.
- Postmortem must include: summary, timeline, RCA, corrective actions, ownership, and follow-up tracker.

Appendix A 	 Example minimal JSON summary schema for benchmark outputs:
```
{
  "run_id": "rwd-20290301-1234",
  "model_id": "rwd/model-v2",
  "commit_hash": "a1b2c3d4",
  "metrics": "accuracy:0.923,bleu:0.45,latency_p95_ms:118",
  "prompt_counts": "tier_a:1200,tier_b:800,tier_c:200",
  "seed": "42",
  "start_time": "2029-03-01T12:34:00Z",
  "end_time": "2029-03-01T12:48:00Z"
}
```

Appendix B — Quick checklists (copy into PR template):
- Model card attached and reviewed.
- Tier A prompt set passes baseline >= required threshold.
- Quantization profile (if used) has acceptance sign-off.
- Canary rollout plan documented and rollback criteria defined.
- Dashboard + alert created for this model.

- Owners (Evaluation Lead + Applied ML) will review this playbook quarterly and after any Sev1 production regression.
- Major changes should be published via a PR and reviewed by the reviewers listed in the metadata.
